jobs.occupation: A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years.
jobs.description:
A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years. The starting date is 01 February 2027 or later by agreement and depending on the candidate’s preferences.

We are seeking a researcher with documented experience in epidemiological research who can independently plan studies, conduct analyses and write scientific papers. We are looking for a future colleague with a clear academic interest in women’s mental health and the motivation to develop their research in this field. Experience in psychiatric epidemiology is a distinct advantage.

The project

The position is funded by a grant from the Wellcome Trust through PROMIS, an international research project on women’s mental health during perimenopause. The project is in its initial phase and will draw on cohort data linked to national registers, in collaboration with researchers in the UK, the USA and Sweden.

The project investigates risk factors for the onset or recurrence of depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders during perimenopause. The work includes epidemiological studies of risk, the development and validation of prediction models, and studies of hormone therapy and mental health outcomes using target trial emulation.

Research tasks

The postdoc will work closely with Principal Investigator Professor Trine Munk-Olsen and the project’s data analyst and participate actively in the international research collaboration. The candidate will have considerable scope to shape research questions, the structure of individual studies, study designs and methodological choices within the framework of the project.

The main tasks are to:

• 
Plan and conduct epidemiological studies using register and cohort data, including preparing study protocols and analysis plans.

• 
Independently perform statistical analyses, interpret results and write scientific papers.

• 
Identify risk factors for mental disorders during perimenopause and contribute to the development and validation of prediction models.

• 
Contribute to studies using target trial emulation to investigate hormone therapy and mental health outcomes.

• 
Together with other project team members, contribute to applications for access to external datasets and to the maintenance, quality assurance, harmonisation and documentation of the datasets used.

• 
Participate in subprojects and undertake tasks within the international collaboration, including coordination, organising project meetings and following up on joint agreements.

The position will involve limited travel. It is primarily research-oriented. Teaching and supervision duties may be included, depending also on the candidate’s interests and preferences.

Expectations of qualifications

The applicant who is hired must have a Ph.D. degree in epidemiology, health sciences, biostatistics or data science with a strong focus on health. Candidates who have not yet completed their Ph.D. may apply if they expect to obtain the degree by the starting date. However, we envisage that, in addition to their Ph.D., the candidate will have at least 1–2 years of research-related experience, for example as a postdoc, research assistant or statistician.

The applicant must have the following qualifications:

• 
A clear academic interest in research on women’s mental health, including the relationships between reproductive life stages and mental disorders.

• 
First authorship of several scientific papers, including documented experience in epidemiological research based on register or cohort data.

• 
Documented experience with advanced epidemiological and statistical methods.

• 
Documented experience and competence in statistical programming, for example in R or Stata.

• 
A documented ability to independently plan studies, prepare study protocols, conduct analyses and write scientific papers.

• 
Good collaboration skills and the ability to take responsibility for tasks and contribute constructively to joint research projects.

• 
The ability to work systematically with data quality, documentation and the maintenance of research data.

• 
Fluency in written and spoken English.

The following would be an advantage but are not requirements:

• 
Experience in psychiatric epidemiology.

• 
Experience in the development or validation of prediction models.

• 
Practical experience with target trial emulation.

• 
Experience in international research collaborations.

• 
Written and spoken Danish, as Danish is the working language of the research unit.

Research environment

The position is based in the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, a growing, dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark. Our research group brings together expertise in psychiatry, psychology, epidemiology and public health. We offer a friendly, inclusive and interdisciplinary working environment where early-career researchers are supported in developing their academic and professional skills. The unit leads several major research projects focusing on perinatal mental health, child and adolescent psychiatry, and early intervention and prevention.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information 

For further information please contact Professor Trine Munk-Olsen, e-mail: tmun@sdu.dk, phone: +45 24 46 62 97.

Application deadline

November 18, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET).

Interviews

Interviews are expected to take place in early December 2026.

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Postdoc is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed postdoc allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Hospitalsringen 90, 5260 Odense S.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
a motivation letter

• 
a detailed CV

• 
degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications

• 
3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file.

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a detailed description of research experience

• 
an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Theoretical Metamaterial Acoustofluidics - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
A 3-year PhD scholarship, starting 1 January 2027 is available in the Department of Physics (DTU Physics) in the field of theoretical metamaterial acoustofluidics supervised by Professor Henrik Bruus, www.staff.dtu.dk/bruus. 

We study the fundamental physics of fluids embedded in elastic solids particularly in the form of metamaterials and actuated by ultrasound through electromechanical transducers. We develop physical models and perform high-fidelity numerical simulations of selected systems often in international collaborations with various experimental groups. The PhD scholarship is part of the theoretical acoustofluidics project "High-performance, metamaterial-based acoustofluidc devices" funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF-FTP). The main research topics are microscale acoustofluidics, elastodynamics, electromechanical actuation, suppression of viscous dissipation by synchronous fluid-wall motion, acoustic resonances in microdevices, acoustic forces on suspended particles and solutions, and acoustic streaming.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will be responsible for 

• developing physical models of acoustofluidic devices with metamaterial walls 
• implementing and performing weak-form FEM simulations of metamaterial acoustofluidic devices
• designing, and numerically testing, optimal metamaterial-based devices for high-performance acoustofluidic nanoparticle handling
We expect that you

• create and critically validate acoustofluidics models relevant for your research project, 
• deliver theoretical and modeling results of high quality,
• participate in team work with independent and original theory/modeling contributions,
• collaborate effectively with experimentalists among the international collaborators, 
• are excited to teach and to learn from other group members,
• communicate your insights and results effectively both orally and in writing,
• work with an outstanding drive and enthusiasm.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Henrik Bruus.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Professor Henrik Bruus, bruus@fysik.dtu.dk. 

You can read more about the research group of Professor Bruus at www.staff.dtu.dk/bruus and about DTU Department of Physics at www.fysik.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

At DTU Physics, we perform research, teaching, and innovation in experimental and theoretical physics with the overall aim to benefit society. We contribute to the transition to sustainable energy via research and innovation in catalysis, Power-to-X, and nuclear energy solutions. We design and develop new functional materials, contribute to advances in geosciences and life sciences, and we develop and exploit quantum physics and quantum technologies

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics Technology Development
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in mass spectrometry and proteomics technology development at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University, Denmark.

The position is available in the Nielsen Laboratory, which focuses on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based technologies to understand regulatory protein states, post-translational modifications (PTMs), and cellular signalling.

We are seeking an ambitious and technically skilled researcher with demonstrated experience in developing, establishing, or optimizing mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies. Candidates should have a strong background in at least one area of proteomics technology development, including LC-MS/MS method development, chromatographic optimization, sample preparation, PTM analysis, or related analytical technologies.

The position offers an exciting opportunity to pursue innovative technology development while taking an active role in building and shaping a growing research group at Aarhus University.

Expected start date and duration of employment

The position is a two-year postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of extension.
The expected start date is 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The successful candidate will join a growing research programme focused on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based proteomics technologies and applying these to fundamental questions in molecular and cellular biology.

Our research integrates state-of-the-art mass spectrometry, quantitative proteomics, analytical method development, peptide and protein chemistry, and PTM biology to investigate how regulatory protein states control cellular function.

A central objective of the position is to develop innovative analytical methodologies that expand the capabilities, sensitivity, robustness, and throughput of modern proteomics. Potential research directions include advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition strategies, quantitative PTM proteomics, chromatographic optimization, automated sample preparation, and novel approaches for studying protein regulation.

The position provides considerable scientific freedom to develop and pursue new technological ideas, with opportunities to establish independent research directions and translate methodological innovations into high-impact scientific publications.

As an early member of a newly established research group at Aarhus University, the successful candidate will also have a unique opportunity to actively contribute to the development of the laboratory's scientific activities, technological capabilities, and future research directions.

Primary responsibilities

• Develop, establish, and optimize innovative mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies.
• Design and independently drive research projects with a strong emphasis on analytical innovation and technological advancement.
• Explore and implement new approaches to improve proteomics sensitivity, quantitative accuracy, reproducibility, and analytical throughput.
• Develop and apply advanced proteomics technologies to investigate PTMs and regulatory protein states.
• Contribute to establishing new experimental workflows and analytical capabilities within the laboratory.
• Collaborate with national and international research partners across proteomics, analytical chemistry, and molecular biology.
• Communicate research findings through publications in leading international scientific journals and presentations at scientific conferences.
• Contribute to the scientific development and continued expansion of the research group, including mentoring junior researchers and developing new collaborative projects.
Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in proteomics, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, or a closely related discipline.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have demonstrated the ability to develop, establish, or substantially improve experimental and analytical methodologies, rather than solely applying established proteomics workflows.

Applicants must demonstrate significant hands-on experience and scientific contributions in at least one of the following areas:

• Mass spectrometry method development: Establishment or optimization of advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition methodologies, including data-independent acquisition (DIA), fragmentation strategies, instrument parameter optimization, or related approaches for improving analytical performance on modern mass spectrometry platforms.
• Liquid chromatography and separation technologies: Development and optimization of chromatographic methodologies for proteomics, including LC gradient design, peptide separation, nanoLC or microflow LC, improved peak capacity, or approaches to enhance sensitivity, robustness, and throughput.
• Proteomics sample preparation and workflow development: Development or substantial optimization of protein and peptide sample preparation methodologies, including automated or high-throughput workflows, digestion strategies, sample clean-up, enrichment techniques, or quantitative proteomics applications.
• Post-translational modification proteomics: Development and optimization of methodologies for PTM enrichment, characterization, or quantitative analysis, including phosphorylation, ADP-ribosylation, ubiquitination, or other regulatory protein modifications.
• Peptide and protein chemistry: Development of innovative approaches involving peptide or protein chemistry, chemical modification, affinity enrichment, selective capture, or related analytical strategies relevant to mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
• Innovative proteomics technologies: Development of other advanced analytical approaches, such as low-input or single-cell proteomics, alternative fragmentation techniques, novel sample processing technologies, or integrated analytical workflows.
Expertise in one of these areas is sufficient. Applicants are not expected to possess experience across all the listed technologies. We particularly welcome researchers with a strong technical specialization who are motivated to expand their expertise into complementary areas of proteomics technology development.

Demonstrated scientific achievements
A central selection criterion will be the applicant's demonstrated contribution to methodological development and technological innovation.

Applicants are expected to document relevant expertise through at least one first-author research publication in which they have made a substantial contribution to the development, establishment, or optimization of an analytical method or experimental technology.

In their application, candidates should identify the publication(s) most relevant to this requirement and briefly describe their personal contributions, the technological challenge addressed, and the methodological advances achieved.

Additional qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage but is not required:

• Proteomics data processing, bioinformatics, quantitative data analysis, or systems biology.
• Advanced computational analysis of LC-MS/MS data, including DIA data processing and statistical evaluation.
• Mammalian cell culture, including experimental perturbations and cellular model systems.
• Handling and processing of biological tissues, clinical samples, or other complex biological materials.
• Development or implementation of laboratory automation and high-throughput experimental workflows.
• Protein biochemistry, molecular biology, or functional studies of protein regulation.
• Programming, scripting, or computational workflow development, including R or Python.
• Experience working across interdisciplinary projects involving analytical technology development and biological applications.
 
Personal qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who:

• Is scientifically ambitious, highly motivated, and driven by developing innovative solutions to challenging analytical problems.
• Demonstrates creativity, initiative, and a strong ability to translate scientific ideas into experimental advances.
• Takes ownership of research projects and has the determination to drive them from initial concept to publication.
• Enjoys solving technical challenges and continuously improving experimental methodologies.
• Thrives in a dynamic research environment where new ideas, technologies, and scientific directions are actively developed.
• Works independently while contributing positively to a collaborative and supportive research environment.
• Has strong scientific communication skills and an interest in developing an independent research profile.

Who we are
The position will be based in the Nielsen Laboratory at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University.

Our research focuses on understanding how dynamic post-translational modification networks regulate protein function and cellular behaviour. We develop and apply innovative mass spectrometry-based technologies to characterize regulatory protein states and uncover fundamental mechanisms controlling cellular function in health and disease.

The laboratory builds on more than 15 years of internationally recognized research in regulatory proteomics, ADP-ribosylation biology, and mass spectrometry-based technology development.

We are currently establishing and expanding our research activities at Aarhus University, combining technological innovation with fundamental biological discovery.

Joining the laboratory at this stage provides a particularly attractive opportunity for a motivated researcher to help build a research environment, influence its technological development, establish new analytical capabilities, and contribute to defining future research priorities.

The group benefits from strong international scientific connections and an interdisciplinary research environment spanning molecular biology, genome stability, structural biology, enzymology, and advanced proteomics.

MBG provides an outstanding interdisciplinary research environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure and a strong commitment to scientific excellence.

More information:
https://mbg.au.dk

What we offer 
We offer:

• A unique opportunity to take an active role in establishing and shaping a growing proteomics research group at Aarhus University.
• Considerable scientific freedom to develop innovative technologies and pursue independent research ideas.
• Access to advanced mass spectrometry and proteomics research infrastructure.
• Opportunities to pioneer analytical workflows and establish technological capabilities with broad scientific applications.
• A research environment where technological innovation, scientific ambition, and independent initiative are strongly encouraged.
• Strong opportunities for high-impact scientific publications, international collaborations, and conference participation.
• Support for career development, scientific networking, and applications for independent research funding.
• Close interaction with national and international researchers working at the forefront of proteomics, PTM biology, and molecular biology.
• A collaborative and supportive environment that values scientific creativity, technical excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Place of work and area of employment 
Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
For further information, please contact:

Professor Michael L. Nielsen

Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics

Aarhus University

Email: mln@mbg.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 23 November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor (tenure track)/Associate Professor in Computational end Generative Design
jobs.description:
Are you interested in scientific computing, artificial intelligence, and how they can automate and enhance design of civil engineering structures? Are you interested in creating societal impact with your research? Then the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering of Aarhus University invites you to apply for this position.

The expected starting date is no later than August 1 2027.

This position is part of the section for Structural Engineering.

• Supervising students at different levels (e.g., multidisciplinary projects, master theses, doctoral theses).
• Conducting research through externally sponsored grants at national and international levels.
• Establishing relevant collaborations with the Danish industry.
• Contributing to the operation of the department.
Your profile
We are looking for a candidate that can enhance the department’s competencies in computational design. The candidate shall hold:

• Engineering background (B.Sc. and M.Sc.).
• Doctoral degree in a relevant field of research.
• High-level proficiency in English.
The following qualifications and experience are required:

• Scientific computing, possibly with different programming languages (e.g., Python, Julia, C#, C++ MATLAB).
• Parametric and algorithmic building design using, e.g., Rhino/Grasshopper tool suite.
• Physics-informed machine learning, generative and agentic AI for building design automation.
• Teaching and developing computational and generative design courses related to structural engineering.
• Supervision of undergraduate and graduate students (B.Sc., M.Sc., and Ph.D. theses).
Candidates must demonstrate potential for outstanding research and teaching. The selected candidate shall demonstrate:

• Some years of post-graduate research and publication experience are required. A pre-existing and growing international research network is expected. Prior collaboration with the Danish innovation ecosystem is desired, but not essential.
• Experience from successful external research collaborations with industry and academia, project management skills. Experience in the attraction of external funding is preferred.
• Research ability documented through rising publication and citation records evidenced by appropriate bibliometric parameters in reputable international peerreviewed journals.
Well-defined research focus and sound strategy to develop a research group.

Who we are
The Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University is a growing engineering environment with a clear vision for the future of the built environment.

Established in 2021, the department today includes more than 100 researchers and educators and around 1.050 students. We conduct research and education within structural engineering, geotechnics, architectural engineering and design, sustainability, construction management, climate adaptation, indoor climate, building materials, and digital technologies.

The construction sector is facing major challenges related to climate, resource consumption, and the way we design and build our cities and buildings.

Through research, education, and collaboration with industry and public-sector partners, we contribute to developing technological solutions that support a more sustainable built environment.

Our research and development activities are closely connected to the needs of industry and society, and many projects are carried out in collaboration with companies, public authorities, and other research environments. This ensures that the knowledge and technologies developed at the department are relevant in practice and create value beyond the university.

Education is a central part of the department’s identity. We offer Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD programmes in engineering and continuously work to improve the connection between research, teaching, and practice.

Across our programmes, students work with real-world challenges, current technologies, and sustainable solutions for the construction sector.

What we offer
We offer an innovative and collaborative teaching and research environment with close interaction between students, researchers, and industry partners. The department provides well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, and access to shared technical facilities. We offer an interdisciplinary environment with national, international, and industrial collaborators. Our academic environment is built on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and professional dialogue. The workplace is characterised by professionalism, flexibility, and a healthy work–life balance. The department is located at Navitas on the waterfront in Aarhus, Denmark

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Navitas, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. The area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Giuseppe Abbiati +45 93 52 17 51, abbiati@cae.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than December 14 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Experienced High Voltage Specialist wanted for Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst
jobs.description:
Do you have at least three years of high voltage experience? At Bravida, you will install circuit breakers, disconnectors and switchboards and help build substations. Here, you will put your experience to use on critical electrical infrastructure projects that help secure Denmark’s power supply and support the green transition.

On behalf of Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst, Career | a JKS Company is recruiting experienced High Voltage Specialists for projects across Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst has secured the framework agreement with Energinet, becoming a regular supplier of high voltage installation work across Zealand and Lolland-Falster. With this agreement and a strong order book, Bravida is expanding the department. You will join the team responsible for building, expanding, refurbishing and maintaining the infrastructure that the power grid of the future relies on.

Installation and construction of high voltage installations
You will work at substations and other high voltage installations, putting your experience into practice. You will take responsibility for your own tasks and work alongside your team to deliver safe, high-quality work.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Installing and replacing circuit breakers, disconnectors and other substation components

• 
Carrying out cable work and working on earthing systems

• 
Working on switchboards, electrical installations and dismantling tasks

• 
Contributing to the construction, refurbishment and maintenance of high voltage installations

• 
Carrying out quality assurance and maintaining documentation

Over time, you will also share your knowledge by helping apprentices and new colleagues get to grips with their tasks.

You bring solid high voltage experience and take responsibility
You are a qualified electrician or have an equivalent electrical qualification, with at least three years of hands-on experience in high voltage work. You are familiar with the tasks described and comfortable working independently. You take initiative, recognise what needs doing and understand that safety is integral to every task.

We are looking for someone who:

• 
Works independently and takes a structured approach

• 
Takes responsibility for the safety and quality of their work

• 
Is proactive, well-presented and works well with others

• 
Is physically fit and comfortable with hands-on work outdoors and at height

• 
Holds a category B driving licence and can provide a criminal record certificate

You must be able to communicate clearly in English and have a valid work permit for Denmark.

A company vehicle to take home and no on-call duties
At Bravida, you will join a team of skilled, dedicated technicians who take pride in their work.

You will work daytime hours with no on-call duties, normally five days a week. Start times depend on the project, and the working week can be discussed. The role is paid hourly, with pay based on qualifications, plus pension contributions and a flexible benefits allowance under the Danish “fritvalgsordning” scheme.

You will have a company vehicle equipped with the tools and equipment you need, which you can take home. Your exact location is therefore less important, provided you are willing to work at different sites across Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

We look forward to hearing from you
If this sounds like the right role for you, please send us your CV. We review applications and invite suitable candidates to interviews on an ongoing basis, and will close the vacancy once the right candidates have been found.

If you have any questions about the role that are not covered in this advertisement, please contact Recruitment Specialist Kristine Askjær on +45 3085 1302.

Please note that, for GDPR reasons, applications submitted directly by email will not be processed or receive a response.

jobs.occupation: Content and Creative Specialist (Part-Time)
jobs.description:
Are you a strong writer with an eye for design and a practical approach to using artificial intelligence?

Can you keep a website fresh, turn ideas into engaging social content, and build workflows that make content production more efficient?

Patiro is looking for a part-time Content and Creative Specialist to manage and develop our content across our website, social media, press releases, and external profiles. You will help us communicate clearly, maintain a consistent brand, and reach the right audiences.

Your responsibilities

You will help us:

• Plan and maintain a content calendar across our channels.

• Write, edit, publish, and update website content, social media posts, press releases, and other communications.

• Keep company listings, directories, and relevant registers accurate and up to date.

• Create visuals and reusable templates in Figma or similar design tools.

• Refine our brand guidelines and apply them consistently across content and design.

• Follow and develop our voice and tone guidelines, adapting communication to different audiences.

• Use artificial intelligence and automation tools, such as Make.com, to improve content workflows, approvals, publishing, and distribution.

• Repurpose content into formats suited to different channels and audiences.

• Improve content discoverability across search engines and artificial intelligence search and answer platforms.

• Track content performance and use the findings to improve topics, formats, and distribution.

• Coordinate with internal experts to ensure content is accurate, relevant, and ready for publication.

What we are looking for

You are someone who:

• Has experience creating and managing content across websites and social media.

• Writes clear, engaging English and can turn complex subjects into accessible stories.

• Has a strong visual eye and practical experience with Figma or similar tools.

• Can share examples of content and creative work you have produced.

• Has hands-on experience using artificial intelligence and automation tools to improve workflows while maintaining editorial quality.

• Understands how content can support awareness, engagement, and action.

• Keeps up with developments in search engine optimisation and content visibility across large language models, generative search, and answer engines.

• Works independently, manages priorities, and takes content from initial idea through publication and review.

• Checks facts carefully and handles sensitive topics with sound judgement.

Technical search optimisation skills are welcome, but are not required. We value strong editorial judgement, creative ability, and the ability to put useful tools into practice.

Additional experience we would value

• Healthcare, clinical research, or patient-facing communications.

• Press releases, media outreach, or corporate communications.

• Content management systems and publishing tools.

• Short-form video creation and editing.

• Community management and audience engagement.

• Content analytics and testing different messages or creative formats.

About the role

You will work closely with our leadership, marketing, and medical teams to build a consistent and credible presence for Patiro. We are looking for someone who can contribute ideas and take ownership of the daily work needed to keep our content relevant and our channels active.

Hours: 5-15 hours per weekStart date: As soon as possible

Send your application, a short introduction, and examples of your writing and visual work to the email below.

Please also share an example of how you have used artificial intelligence or automation to improve a content workflow, including your role and the result.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Apply via this e-mail

careers@patiro.com

Reach out to us if you have any questions related to the open positions.

jobs.description:
Who you are

Elsker du at arbejde i de sene dagstimer? Ja, så er du måske vores nye kollega i Fulfilment Operation.

I IKEA har Fulfilment Operation afdelingerne hver dag ansvaret for at varehuset er velopfyldt og klar til vores kunder, hvad end det handler om at tømme lastbilerne, hejse varer til højlageret eller ligge varer på plads på salgspladserne.

Vi forventer at du:

- Er i god fysisk form og kan håndtere tunge løft

- Trives med at arbejde i de tidlige morgentimer

- Er struktureret, har evnen til at have overblik og fokus på orden

- Kan tale engelsk og har lyst til kommunikere med mange kollegaer samt at arbejde i et team

- Det vil være en fordel hvis du har et truckcertifikat, men dette er ikke et krav

A day in your life with us

As a Fulfilment Operation Co-worker, you play an important role in IKEA’s sales and customer satisfaction, ensuring that customers never leave empty-handed when shopping for home furnishings.

Your tasks will include:

• Stocking furniture and home accessories such as plates, sofas, lamps, etc., using pallet jacks, manual labor, and possibly forklifts/stackers

• Ensuring accurate inventory through daily counts

• Daily handover to our sales colleagues after operations

• Daily maintenance of the department, including tidying up

• Daily maintenance of machines.

Together as a Team

You’ll be part of an international team of both full-time and part-time employees, all working toward the same goal. We ensure efficient stocking in the store and provide great service to customers, even though we don’t have direct customer contact. We work closely with other departments, giving you experience in collaborating with many different people. We work at a fast pace but have a strong team spirit, supporting each other and working together. There’s room for you to be exactly who you are. We provide proper training so you can feel confident and competent in the role.

Apply now!

If you have any questions please contact our Fulfillment Operations Team Leader Anders Jensen (anders.jensen3@ingka.ikea.com). Please notice that we do not receive applications via e-mail but only through our recruitment portal.

Further information

• The position is for an average of 30 hours per week.

• Your working hours may vary depending on operational needs, primarily in the evening and night from 18OM-02.00AM

AM. You should expect to work every other weekend, both Saturday and Sunday. You can provide input for the work schedule.

• Salary within IKEA’s wage framework for warehouse/logistics, including pension and flexible benefits, as well as shift allowances.

• Other working conditions follow the HK union agreement for salaried employees.

• We offer various employee benefits such as health insurance, massage program, canteen, staff discount, partner discount schemes, annual gift, and bonus program.

• As part of the hiring process, a criminal record check will be required.

• Desired start date is as soon as possible

• We conduct interviews continuously and reserve the right to close the job posting once we have received enough qualified candidates.

Just like our homes, our talents are diverse, and at IKEA we have a passion for people. Some may lose confidence when applying if they don’t meet all the qualifications, but you are very welcome to apply anyway. We want to get to know you, and there are many opportunities at IKEA based on interest, skills, and experience. We hope you’ll join the journey and look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.description:
**Job Description

**_Are you ready to play a key role in transforming resource allocation at one of the leading financial institutions? Join our Enterprise Cost Steering team to lead initiatives that improve financial health through strategic cost optimization. This position offers a unique opportunity to influence cost efficiency strategies Group-wide.

_**What You Will Be Doing

**As an Experienced Consultant in Enterprise Cost Steering, you will support the executive leadership team with insights and recommendations to optimize cost structures. Working closely with Finance teams, Procurement, Support functions, and Business Units, you will identify cost-optimizing opportunities and implement best practices that strengthen our financial foundation.

• Own, drive, coordinate and execute end-to-end cost efficiency initiatives across the Group, including planning, tracking progress and managing delivery against agreed milestones

• Apply strong critical thinking by questioning assumptions and provide well-reasoned recommendations

• Leverage data analytics to conduct comprehensive cost analysis and identify cost efficiency opportunities

• Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to design and implement cost steering frameworks, ensuring clear governance, roles and responsibilities

• Translate complex data into actionable insights for senior leadership

• Act as trusted partner providing expert guidance on strategic cost initiatives

• Build and maintain dashboards and tools to support ongoing cost analysis, generating actionable insights, reporting and decision-making

• Facilitate workshops to align stakeholders and build consensus on initiatives and drive agreed actions to completion

**About You

**

• Strong consulting and project management background, with experience delivering strategic solutions in complex organisations

• Solid experience in enterprise-level cost steering or strategic cost management

• Excellent problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail

• Proven ability to independently manage initiatives from ideation through execution, including defining scope, plans, milestones, dependencies and delivery risks

• Strong critical thinking skills with ability to challenge assumptions

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management, with the ability to engage, influence and build trust across all levels while maintaining alignment, accountability and momentum

• Advanced skills in data analysis, reporting and visualisation tools

• Master's degree in finance, economics, business administration or similar

You thrive in dynamic environments with evolving priorities and demonstrate collaborative teamwork alongside quantitative expertise to support strategic decision-making.

**What We Offer You

**You will join a supportive team that values collaboration and professional growth. We offer hybrid working with 3 to 4 days per week in the office to promote knowledge sharing and culture building. You will have opportunities to develop your expertise while making meaningful contributions to our financial health and cost efficiency initiatives.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**We would love to hear from you if this opportunity excites you. Please reach out to Hadis Atighi at kho@danskebank.dk for any questions about the role. We process applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply sooner rather than later.

We look forward to receiving your application!

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join our High-Performance Development team in Denmark in a role focused on Improving and maintaining our power plant control software solution that is deployed to SGRE wind farms all over the world.

Your day may start with investigating a support case, perform remote troubleshooting and conduct detailed event analysis of power plant operations to identify and resolve software or configuration issues.

Afterwards you would resume to your regular software development task in the agile development team, with daily scrums and develop high-quality code including unit- and automated integration tests to ensure correct behavior.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Develop/maintain. C# .NET based platform that supports real-time control

• Design and develop data services that serve, process and store large data amounts within wind farms.

• Relentless focus on cyber solutions.

• Develop configuration validation, monitoring and tooling

• Clarify and mature requirements

• Contribute to planning

What You Bring

• Bachelors or Masters degree in Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline, preferably combined with relevant professional engineering experience.

• C# and automated testing. Experience with CI/CD practices, agile development methodologies, C++ and Python language experience is appreciated as well.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

About the Team

You will join the Development team in Denmark, where Software Developer/Engineers collaborate to constantly improve wind farm control and power plant solutions.

Knowledge sharing, peer reviews, and open collaboration are an integral part of the team's way of working. At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. jobs.occupation: Global Benefits Consultant
jobs.description:
Exciting opportunity to join our Integrated & Global Services (IGS) line of business as an Associate Manager of Global Employee Benefits, based in our Nærum office, just outside of Copenhagen, Denmark. We offer an attractive workplace with a balanced mix of office and remote working. This role will be focused on managing and delivering large, strategic client engagements to multinational clients concerning their health and risk benefits globally. There may be a need to travel as needed for client and internal business needs.

Operating in the global marketplace means multinational companies face a variety of different business, cultural, language and regulatory environments. Our IGS line of business helps these companies navigate the challenges of multi-country complexity based on context knowledge of trends and innovative multi-client solutions. In particular, we help multinational companies develop global/cross-border solutions that meet the needs of both local and headquarter management in the design, establishment, financing, operation, oversight and monitoring of their compensation and benefit programs around the world.  In doing so, we work closely with our local offices in other geographies, as well as subject matter experts in other segments.

Our Global Benefits Management (GBM) business has a particular focus around the coordination of insured employee benefits, and also has the breadth to consider other Benefits and Total Reward aspects as demanded by our clients. The GBM business is one of the fastest growing areas of our business with an expanding marketplace and exciting, evolving client needs. As an Associate Manager in our GBM delivery team, you will play a key part in this growth story, taking a lead role in delivering across multiple focus areas and geographies to some of our biggest multinational clients.

The Role

• Manage multiple client engagements.

• Contribute to client delivery teams, providing guidance and training to junior team members as needed, and take responsibility for client deliverables

• Operate on teams providing advice on global health, risk and other benefits.

• Engage with clients, building relationships and provide consistent, superior project delivery.

• Manage large International consulting client engagements:

• Coordinate teams and promote effective working

• Develop project plans for execution of large, global engagements

• Ensure project managers are maintaining team progress against goals

• Build relationships internally and collaborate effectively on cross-functional and cross-regional teams.

• Partnering with regional/ local Health & Benefits, International consultants and regional/local geography teams

• Contribute to relationships with internal and external sources to maximize the activity on key target accounts

What you’ll bring

• 3+ years of project management, client facing or consulting experience

• Employee benefits experience, preferably with health and risk benefits, Rewards or HR expertise (across multiple countries is a bonus)

• Fluent in English language (Fluency in a Scandinavian language is a bonus).

• Track record of success in managing client contact relationships, demonstrating ability to communicate clearly in a client-facing role

• Ability to work both on their own and with client teams, including virtual work teams with members in different geographic locations.

• Understanding of the nuances of working across borders, with different cultures and with multinational organizations,

• The ability to deal positively with change and comfort working in a global environment.

• Strong organizational abilities and flexibility to work in a fast-paced, performance driven environment managing multiple project priorities.

• Interest and aptitude in keeping abreast of latest developments in global compensation/benefits approaches and contributing to the development of new tools and approaches.

• The ability to use Microsoft Excel to manipulate and analyze data, as well as a working knowledge of Microsoft PowerPoint

• Higher educational background, e.g., a master’s or BA degree from business or numeric from a university or Business School

• Ability to travel on as needed basis

Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to equal employment opportunity and provide application, interview and workplace adjustments and accommodations to all applicants. If you foresee any barriers, from the application process through to joining WTW, please email candidate.helpdesk@wtwco.com
